title: ReadyHealth – Active in Everyday Life: A Mobile Prevention App to Promote Physical Activity, Healthy Eating (Prevention of Deficiency and Malnutrition), and Stress and Resource Management – Effectiveness of the 6-Month Digital, Cross-Domain Prevention Program: A Prospective Before-and-After Observational Study
summary:
More and more people are suffering from non-contagious diseases. These include, for example, cardiovascular diseases and diabetes. These conditions often result from a lack of physical activity, an unhealthy diet, and chronic stress. This poses major challenges for the healthcare system.
In a work and living environment that is becoming increasingly digital, many existing prevention programs are reaching their limits. These programs are often tied to specific locations and times. As a result, they fail to reach many people, are not used regularly, or do not lead to lasting changes in daily life.
People with limited knowledge about health and low levels of education are particularly affected.  This also includes people with low incomes, older adults, young adults, and people with immigrant backgrounds.
That is why digital prevention programs are becoming increasingly important.  They can reach many people, integrate well into daily life, and are based on scientific evidence.
This study protocol describes an investigation of the Fitness Nation | ReadyHealth – Active in Everyday Life program. It is a digital prevention program designed in accordance with the guidelines of statutory health insurance. Particular attention is paid to ensuring that the content is scientifically sound, that participants receive individualized support, and that the quality of the program is guaranteed.
The program combines the topics of exercise, nutrition, and stress management. It is supplemented by digital coaching that supports participants in their daily lives (including through the use of behavior change techniques).
conditions: Digital, cross-sectoral prevention with a particular focus on promoting physical activity, healthy eating, and stress and resource management

interventions.name: Users of the digital prevention program are surveyed a total of three times: at the start, after using the program, and in a follow-up assessment six months later

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
People who are physically inactive, have poor dietary habits, or experience stress-related strain in their daily lives, but do not have any medical conditions in these areas that require treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
•    Acute conditions: Existing epilepsy, advanced pregnancy, or acute febrile infections.
•    Clinical conditions: Diagnosed eating disorders (anorexia, bulimia) or severe obesity (BMI > 40) requiring close medical or therapeutic supervision.
•    Cardiovascular risks: Acute cardiovascular diseases that preclude exercise for preventive purposes.
•    Psychosocial crises: Acute psychological instability or crises that go beyond the scope of general stress prevention.
